name: Local ladder 1: CLIP reranking, part plans and cleaner data, measured on the Mac
description: No more GPU rental. Glimmer v3/v4 produce valid meshes 76-80% of the time but only about 15-20% are recognisable, and more of the same data did not help (docs/12-proof-ladder.md, final result 4 Nov 2026). This PRD builds the tools to test three cheaper levers locally on the M3 Max (MLX, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, already cached): (1) pick among samples by CLIP image-text score instead of the medoid, which favours the average box; (2) a part plan before the mesh (connected components with bounding boxes, written inside reasoning tags); (3) cleaner data (drop near-boxes and near-duplicates). Every lever is measured by the same automatic metric (CLIP score and caption retrieval on rendered views), replacing eyeball judgement.

userStories.title: render_views.mjs: render each text mesh from four angles to PNG files

userStories.title: clip_score.py: caption-image similarity and caption retrieval with an injectable embedder
userStories.description: As the experimenter, I want one automatic measure of 'does this mesh look like its caption' so that recognisability stops being my eyeball guess.
steps: Create scripts/clip_score.py with pure functions: `cosine(a, b)`; `mesh_score(view_vecs, text_vec)` = mean cosine over the views, times 100; `retrieval_ranks(score_matrix)` where score_matrix[i][j] is the score of mesh i against caption j and the true caption of mesh i is caption i, returning the 1-based rank of the true caption for each mesh (ties count against the mesh); `recall_at(ranks, k)`.

Add class `ClipEmbedder(model_id='openai/clip-vit-base-patch32')` with `images(paths) -> list[list[float]]` and `text(captions) -> list[list[float]]`, L2-normalised. Import torch, PIL and transformers only inside its methods, load with local_files_only=True, and if torch is missing raise RuntimeError naming the manual install command `.venv/bin/pip install torch pillow`. Use the CPU (or mps if available); batch the images.

Add `score_folder(views_dir, items, embedder, views=4)` where items is [{name, caption}]: returns {name: score} for every name whose view files exist, skipping the others. It must work with any object that has images() and text(), so tests pass a fake.

userStories.title: rerank_samples.py: compare first, medoid, CLIP and oracle picks on existing samples
userStories.description: As the experimenter, I want to know, for free, whether Glimmer already produces recognisable meshes that the medoid rule throws away.
steps: Create scripts/rerank_samples.py with two subcommands. `prepare --samples FILE --out-dir DIR`: read rows {caption, picked, answers} (give each row id p000, p001.. by line order when it has no id), validate every answer with mesh_validate.validate, and write DIR/candidates.jsonl with rows {name: '<id>_<k>', id, k, caption, text} for the valid answers only (text = mesh_validate.extract of the answer), plus DIR/prompts.json [{id, caption, n_valid}].

`score --out-dir DIR --views-dir VDIR`: build ClipEmbedder (or the embedder a test injects through a function argument), score every candidate with clip_score.score_folder, then for each prompt compute four picks among its valid candidates: first (lowest k), medoid (mesh_generate.pick_best on the original answers), clip (highest score; tie -> lowest k) and oracle (also highest score; kept as the ceiling, identical to clip for a single scorer, so report it as 'clip' and drop oracle if that is simpler, saying so in the doc). Prompts with no valid candidate count as a miss for every rule.

For each rule report: valid picks, mean CLIP score of the picks, caption retrieval recall@1 and recall@5 of the picked meshes against all prompt captions (clip_score.retrieval_ranks). Write DIR/rerank_report.json and DIR/rerank_report.md (a small table) and DIR/sheet_medoid.jsonl and DIR/sheet_clip.jsonl (rows {name, text} for preview_mesh.mjs).

Refuse --out-dir inside data/, out/ or eval/ (reuse proof_data._protected_folder). Write tests/py/test_rerank_samples.py with a fixture tests/fixtures/local/samples.jsonl (3 prompts x 3 answers, one answer invalid, one prompt with no valid answer), fake view files in tmp_path and a fake embedder that makes a specific non-medoid candidate the best: assert the clip pick differs from the medoid pick there, the report numbers, and the protected-folder refusal.
acceptanceCriteria: prepare writes only valid candidates, named <id>_<k>, and prompts.json counts them (asserted)
score picks the highest-scoring candidate per prompt and a test shows it can differ from the medoid pick (asserted)
rerank_report.json has, for each of first, medoid and clip: valid, mean_clip, r_at_1, r_at_5, and a prompt with no valid answer lowers valid for every rule (asserted)
--out-dir inside data/, out/ or eval/ exits non-zero (asserted)

userStories.title: mesh_parts.py: split a mesh into parts and write a part plan
userStories.description: As the experimenter, I want each training mesh described as a short list of parts with boxes and colours so that the model can be taught to plan the object before writing triangles.
steps: Create scripts/mesh_parts.py working on the text format (glb_to_text.parse_text / to_text). `components(verts, tris)`: connected components of triangles that share a vertex (union-find); also treat identical vertex coordinates as shared so duplicated seam vertices do not split a part.

`parts(text, max_parts=12, min_tris=2)`: one part per component with {tris, colour (most common face colour), bbox (min x y z, max x y z, ints 0..63)}. Components with fewer than min_tris triangles are merged into the part whose bbox centre is nearest; if more than max_parts remain, merge the smallest into its nearest neighbour until max_parts. Order parts by bbox min (y, then z, then x) so the plan reads bottom-up.

`plan_text(parts)`: one line per part, `part N #rrggbb x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1 tN` (N from 1, tN the triangle count). `reorder(text, parts)`: rewrite the mesh so each part's vertices are contiguous and its faces follow, part by part in plan order, with the canonical sorted order (glb_to_text.sort_text rules: vertices by z,y,x, faces by lowest index) inside each part and colour groups restarted per part. The geometry must be unchanged.

Write tests/py/test_mesh_parts.py with fixtures in tests/fixtures/local/: a table (top slab + 4 separate legs = 5 parts), a single cube (1 part), a mesh with a 1-triangle speck (merged), and one with 15 separate tiny boxes (merged down to max_parts). Assert part counts, bboxes, the plan line format by regex, and that reorder keeps the same multiset of triangles as coordinate triples and the result passes mesh_validate.validate.
acceptanceCriteria: The table fixture gives 5 parts and the single cube 1 part (asserted)
Specks below min_tris are merged and no more than max_parts parts are ever returned (asserted)
Every plan line matches `^part \d+ #[0-9a-f]{6}( \d+){6} t\d+$` (asserted)
reorder preserves the triangle multiset as coordinate triples and the output validates (asserted on every fixture)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: local_ab_data.py: four dataset arms (base, plan, clean, clean+plan) from one split
userStories.description: As the experimenter, I want the same train/holdout split written in four variants so that each lever is measured against the same baseline and nothing else changes.
steps: Create scripts/local_ab_data.py. CLI: `--objects corpus/combined2_objects.jsonl --split corpus/combined2_split.json --out-dir DIR --max-lines 300 --orientations 2 --max-train 0 --holdout-n 40 --seed 1`. --max-train N > 0 keeps a seeded random N train objects (the Mac is slower than the GPU); --holdout-n keeps a seeded random subset of the holdout ids. The same chosen ids are used by every arm.

`clean(objects)`: drop near-boxes (mesh with 12 or fewer triangles that forms one part per mesh_parts.parts and whose triangles all lie on its bbox faces) and near-duplicates (same vertex count, same triangle count and bbox within 2 units on each axis as an object kept earlier; keep the first). Return (kept, dropped) where dropped lists {id, reason}. Clean applies to train objects only; holdout is never filtered.

Arms: `base` = proof_unseen.build with sort=True; `plan` = same objects, but every assistant message (train and valid) is THINK_OPEN + '
' + plan_text + '
' + THINK_CLOSE + '

' + reorder(mesh) using mesh_parts on the already rotated and sorted text; `clean` = base after clean(); `clean_plan` = plan after clean(). Import THINK_OPEN and THINK_CLOSE from tags; never type the tags. Each arm goes to DIR/<arm>/ with train.jsonl, valid.jsonl, targets.json (holdout {id, caption, mesh}, mesh always without the plan) in proof_unseen's layout. DIR/manifest.json records the ids, the counts per arm and the dropped list.

Refuse --out-dir inside data/, out/ or eval/. Write tests/py/test_local_ab_data.py with a tiny objects/split fixture in tests/fixtures/local/ (include one near-box and one near-duplicate): the four arm folders exist, the holdout ids are identical in all arms, clean arms lack the near-box and duplicate, plan arm assistant messages start with THINK_OPEN and the part after THINK_CLOSE validates, targets.json meshes contain no plan, and the protected-folder refusal.
acceptanceCriteria: All four arms share the same holdout ids and targets (asserted)
clean drops the near-box and the near-duplicate from train with reasons, and never touches holdout (asserted)
Plan-arm completions are THINK_OPEN + plan + THINK_CLOSE + mesh using the constants from scripts/tags.py, and the mesh part validates (asserted; the literal tags appear nowhere in the new files)
--out-dir inside data/, out/ or eval/ exits non-zero (asserted)

userStories.title: local_eval.py: one comparison table across arms and a verdict
userStories.description: As the experimenter, I want each arm scored on validity, CLIP match, caption retrieval and geometric match to the held-out reference, side by side, with a pre-agreed rule that says which lever helped.
steps: Create scripts/local_eval.py. Input: `--arm NAME=SAMPLES.jsonl` (repeatable), `--targets targets.json`, `--work-dir DIR`. For every arm reuse rerank_samples (prepare and score, with its injectable embedder) so candidates are rendered and scored the same way; the render step is a callable argument (default: run `node scripts/render_views.mjs` via subprocess) so tests can fake it.

Per arm compute: any_valid (prompts with at least one valid sample), sample_valid (valid samples / all samples), loop_or_cap (samples with finish 'length' or 'loop'), and for the clip pick and the medoid pick: mean_clip, r_at_1, r_at_5, and mean fscore against the target mesh (mesh_quality.fscore; 0 for a miss). For plan arms also plan_parse (share of samples whose plan lines all match the mesh_parts format).

Verdict, written into the report exactly as rules: an arm 'beats base' when its clip-pick mean_clip is at least 1.0 higher than base AND its r_at_5 is not lower AND its any_valid is at most 5 percentage points lower; otherwise 'no gain'. Also state whether the clip pick beats the medoid pick within each arm by the same mean_clip rule. Never round away a negative difference.

Write DIR/compare.json and DIR/compare.md (one table, arms as rows, then the verdict lines). Write tests/py/test_local_eval.py with two tiny fake arms built from fixtures, a fake renderer that only creates files and a fake embedder that favours one arm: assert the table columns, the verdict for both outcomes (beats and no gain) and that a negative difference is shown with its sign.
acceptanceCriteria: compare.json has, per arm, any_valid, sample_valid, loop_or_cap and, for clip and medoid picks, mean_clip, r_at_1, r_at_5, fscore (asserted)
The verdict follows the stated rule; tests cover a 'beats base' case and a 'no gain' case (asserted)
Rendering and embedding are injected, so the tests start no browser and load no model (asserted by using fakes that record calls)

userStories.title: local_run.sh and docs/13-local-ladder.md: one command per experiment
userStories.description: As the owner, I want two commands, `rerank` and `ab`, that run the whole local experiment in order and print what they will cost in time before starting, with a dry run to check them.
steps: Create scripts/local_run.sh in the style of scripts/proof_run.sh. `rerank [--samples artifacts/glimmer-v4/gen_v4.samples.jsonl] [--workdir DIR]`: rerank_samples prepare -> node scripts/render_views.mjs -> rerank_samples score -> node scripts/preview_mesh.mjs on sheet_medoid.jsonl and sheet_clip.jsonl -> print rerank_report.md.

`ab [--workdir DIR] [--max-train 600] [--iters 1000] [--arms base,plan,clean,clean_plan] [--model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct]`: local_ab_data.py once, then for each arm in order: mlx_lm lora (same flags and learning-rate guard as proof_run.sh: lr 3e-5, refuse above 1e-4 without --force-lr; max-seq large enough for plan + mesh), local_gen.py on that arm's targets.json, and finally local_eval.py over all arms and print compare.md. Each step skips itself when its output already exists, so an interrupted run resumes. Before starting, print the plan: arms, train rows per arm, iterations, and the line 'time per arm: not measured yet' unless DIR/timings.json from an earlier arm exists, in which case use it. Append each step's wall time to DIR/timings.json.

Both commands refuse a --workdir inside data/, out/ or eval/, default to a new folder under /tmp, never call runpodctl or any network service, and support --dry-run which only echoes the commands. Write tests/py/test_local_run.py that runs both commands with --dry-run in a temp workdir and checks the commands appear in order with the arms, that an lr above 1e-4 is refused without --force-lr, that a protected workdir is refused, and that no 'runpodctl' string occurs in the script.

Write docs/13-local-ladder.md: why (the plateau at 76-80% valid and 15-20% recognisable), the three levers, the metric definitions, the verdict rule from local_eval.py, the manual gates (install torch and pillow, download the CLIP model, run rerank, run ab), what a 0.5B proxy can and cannot tell us about Glimmer, and empty result tables marked 'not measured'. Add one line pointing to it in docs/HANDOVER.md under the top note and in INDEX.md if it lists docs.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Ralph builds and tests the tools with tiny fixtures and fake embedders and generators. It never downloads a model, never installs torch, never trains, never starts mlx_lm or a CLIP model, and never runs runpodctl. The real runs are manual gates listed below. Do not edit existing scripts: new behaviour goes in new files that import from them.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

chromium: Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently

manualGates: Owner installs the scorer once: `.venv/bin/pip install torch pillow` and downloads openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 to the Hugging Face cache (about 600 MB)
Owner runs `bash scripts/local_run.sh rerank` on artifacts/glimmer-v4/gen_v4.samples.jsonl (free, minutes) and reads whether CLIP picks beat medoid picks
Owner runs `bash scripts/local_run.sh ab` (hours on the Mac: four small MLX LoRA arms) and reads the comparison table and verdict before deciding anything about Glimmer
